task_goal: Construct a deep learning model to predict proximal polyadenylation site usage from synthetic DNA regulatory sequences measured by massively parallel reporter assays (MPRA).
task_requirements: The model should take DNA sequences surrounding polyadenylation signals as input and predict proximal polyadenylation usage ratio as a regression task.

task_dataset.description: Dataset derived from the APARENT massively parallel reporter assay for alternative polyadenylation modeling. Each sample contains a synthetic DNA sequence with engineered upstream/downstream mutations around the polyadenylation signal and experimentally measured proximal cleavage usage statistics.
task_dataset.key_constraints: Input sequences are fixed-length DNA regulatory sequences (~186 nt) composed of A/C/G/T characters only. The target variable is a continuous proximal polyadenylation usage ratio ranging from 0 to 1. Test set has been reserved for evaluation, so you only need to split the data into train/validation sets.
